purpose: Test transfer of source-only native group relevance on original grammatical minimal pairs, and falsify orthographic versus grammatical source-group hypotheses with fixed new counterfactual contexts.
budget: Existing shared gpu-0, two CPU threads,1800-second initial bounded run; no paid resource, training or package changes.
source_rule: For each SAE seed and each of three paradigms, choose among its12 fixed source NMF groups the largest mean grammatical good-minus-bad margin decrement on the first64 original pairs, minus the average decrement on the other two paradigms. Ties use the lower componentID. Save all candidates and selection before any target grammar intervention or any held-pair model outcome. No threshold or target-based source choice.
scope: Original sentences, pairIDs and whole-sentence good-vs-bad logprob margin on three of67 BLiMP paradigms. Native deletion at the end of the official shared one-prefix field is the specified intervention; not the original unedited full67 benchmark. First64 rows per paradigm select source groups only; remaining936 positive rows and first64 held rows of each other paradigm evaluate frozen source/target group operations. All3000 pairs parsed/tokenized before inference; held model outcomes start only after source selection freeze. The natural R24 group fit remains fixed/exposed, while these new original pairs test transfer within fixed grammar templates and the same model. Shared seed cycles are dependent. Full raw and rank1/2 ridge fits use only the original natural discovery rows; controlled authored language contexts are a separate hypothesis test. No concept-identity, human annotation or main-conference acceptance claim is assumed.
